summary:
Conclusion: all six "should" findings (T1 to T6) from the first check are gone in /home/user/ppolppol-fix-thin. Each one was reproduced on the state before the repair and is absent now. Each has a check that fails when the fix is reverted, except T6, which was a picture. I found nothing at "must" or "should" level, so the lane can go ahead.

Three things remain. The biggest is an owner decision: the repair fills the band of plain sky the thin bank left (T1) with three extra large clouds. That makes the sky between about 0.9 and 1.4 s noticeably denser than the "sparse clouds" design, and the brief said that should not change. The other two are small: the bank colour plus an overlapping new cloud covers 52.8 to 54.3 % of the screen in some weathers, and one check in the guard is loose enough to let a two-band cover pass.

What I did:
- I copied the first-fix tree (check-thin/fixed) and base b287a11 and re-ran the first checker's mutants on them. On the first-fix tree with its own test, mB (panel in front of the room), mC (gradient reverted) and mD (box-shadow reverted) passed step 0, and mW (8 s wall-clock wait) failed with "덮개 @ NaN". That reproduces T3, T4 and T5.
- I took composited screenshots of the first fix stepped with debugStep. They reproduce T1: at 360x740 navy reaches 92.1 % at 1.08 s and stays above 90 % for 0.18 s; the whole 1280 window reaches 97.6 %. They also reproduce T2: the side and gap columns jump 27 to 36 per channel in one row, navy to black.
- On the repaired tree I measured 27 looks across 6 sizes, every hour (dawn, day, dusk, night) and every weather. Results:
  - On phones and on every canvas, no frame passes the opening frame's share and no canvas frame reaches 90 %.
  - The outside cover steps at most 5 to 6 per channel between rows, with no straight line, and the 1280 side area no longer flips in one frame.
  - The colour switch stays invisible: about 1.88 s, 0 px of sky band visible, 0 errors.
- I looked at the pictures myself around the switch at 1280 day clear, 1280 dusk rain and 360 dusk rain, and in base / first fix / now rows at 360 day clear.
- I wrote 13 mutants of my own and confirmed BOOT_ONLY step 0 passes 5 times in 5.

Suites: npm test 0 failed. test-export first failed with ENOSPC because the root volume was full, then passed 46/0 with TMPDIR on /dev/shm. Font check `stale: none`. Smoke I 31/0, smoke A 74/0. The full intro-shots run passes step 0 and then dies at the step 1 12 s title wait. A control run on an untouched b287a11 copy dies at the same place, so there is no verdict because of load (load average 8 to 12).

No player-facing text, sound or 2D code changed. The new CSS variables are cleared at cleanup, a resize in the middle of the descent keeps one sky (draw calls 20, one switch), and the gap clouds are disposed with the sky.

Note: the scratch volume (/) ran out of space during this check (about 12 MB free, `resv_strict`). Bulk working files (tree copies, mutant copies, frame folders, the browser profile) went to /dev/shm/recheck-thin and were deleted at the end. Results, logs and the picked pictures are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/779b4de3-ceb6-5233-b661-33f83b7682a5/scratchpad/final/recheck-thin/ (notes.md, out/, pics/).

problems.title: T1 is fixed by adding three large clouds; the sky between 0.9 and 1.4 s is visibly denser than the sparse-clouds design
problems.where: js/scene3d.js CLOUD.gap (line 4318) and buildSky (lines 4392-4394); intro 0.9 to 1.4 s; all sizes
problems.what: The repair puts three near-layer clouds (the same art as the existing near clouds) into the band the bank cap opened. This removes the near-full-screen navy moment. The cost: the descent now shows four to six big clouds at once between 0.9 and 1.4 s, where base and the first fix showed one or two small ones. The opening frame also shows a cloud top at the bottom right where base showed the old bank's puffy top. The brief listed the sparse clouds as something not to change, and the first checker offered this option ((c)) only as an owner decision. The repair report and docs section 9 say so.
problems.evidence: pics/r-360-day-base-first-now.png has three rows at 0.3 to 2.1 s: base, first fix, now. Compare the 1.0 to 1.3 s columns. pics/r-360-dusk-rain-now.png shows the same at dusk rain. Measured share of the screen covered by one colour (opening frame first, then the largest after it): 360x740 day clear 73.9 % / 73.9 %; first fix 92.1 % (from out/cur.jsonl, out/first.jsonl).
problems.suggested_fix: The owner looks at the pictures and chooses. (a) Keep the three clouds. (b) Use fewer or smaller clouds: the repair agent measured that one or two clouds peak at 84 to 88 %. (c) Go back to the first fix's plain-sky moment.

problems.title: Bank colour plus an overlapping new cloud covers just over half the screen in some weathers; the guard's <50 % bound checks only clear-weather looks
problems.where: js/scene3d.js CLOUD.gap; tools/intro-shots.js bootPass bodyMax < 0.5 check
problems.what: The new clouds use the bank's body colour. When one overlaps the bank's top, pixels of that one colour cover a little over half the screen. The bank alone stays at about 40 %. Visually this is a cloud above a band, not one flat field, but it misses the brief's 'never half the screen' aim. The guard checks only 13h clear and 18h rain at 412/1280, where the value is 48.3 to 48.5 %, a margin of 1.5 points.
problems.evidence: From out/cur.jsonl, the largest bank-colour share on the canvas: 360x740 rain, snow and dawn snow 52.8 %; 360 drizzle 51.9 %; 320x568 dusk rain 54.3 %, night snow 53.9 %; 412 51.3 %; 430 night snow 50.9 %. The clear looks are 45.6 to 49.2 %. The repair report lists this under 'left'.
problems.suggested_fix: Move the lowest gap cloud (q[0] = 0.3) a little higher or to the side so it does not overlap the bank top, or accept it and state the measured share in docs section 9.

problems.title: The cover-paint check allows half-size steps, so a two-band cover passes everywhere and a one-band cover passes on phones
problems.where: tools/intro-shots.js bootPass paint check: f - prev <= 0.5
problems.what: T4's new check reads real screenshot columns and catches reverting the CSS gradient, the box-shadow, or the mix order. But its 'no straight line' rule only rejects a jump larger than half the navy-to-panel difference in one row. With SKY.steps = 2 the cover has two half-size steps: about 7/11/18 per channel by day, 13/5/9 at dusk. These read as two faint horizontal edges across the 1280 side covers, and step 0 passes. With SKY.steps = 1 step 0 fails only at 1280 (rounding pushes the step above 0.5); the phone pass passes.
problems.evidence: Mutant k3b (SKY.steps = 2): exit 0 (out/mut-k3b.log). Mutant k3 (SKY.steps = 1): only the 1280 side and gap columns fail, the 360 to 412 pass is clean (out/mut-k3.log). The shipped cover steps at most 5 to 6 per channel between rows (out/cur.jsonl stepPreMax).
problems.suggested_fix: Bound the per-row step at about 0.25 of the difference (6 bands give about 0.17), or check the largest per-channel step directly (for example at most 8).

problems.title: Wide-screen whole window stays at or above 90 % one colour longer than base, though never above its own opening frame
problems.where: css/intro.css .intro-hole side covers at 1280x800; 0.9 to 1.25 s
problems.what: At 1280x800 the navy side covers are over half the window. The largest single-colour share in the whole window never goes above the opening frame (92.1 to 92.6 %), and the canvas never reaches 90 %. But after 0.9 s the window stays at 90 % or more for 0.22 to 0.37 s, against 0.13 to 0.25 s in base, where the full-height bank broke up the scene column. Night is the same as base at the peak (94.0 % against 93.9 %, the dark under-cloud moment at 1.98 s). The repair report and docs section 9 state this.
problems.evidence: From out/cur.jsonl (whole window): 1280 day clear >=90 % for 0.37 s, dusk rain 0.23 s, dawn clear 0.37 s, day snow 0.22 s, night rain 0.37 s. From out/base.jsonl: day clear 0.13 s, dusk rain 0.13 s, night rain 0.25 s. Opening frames: base 91.9 to 93.2 %, now 92.1 to 92.6 %.
problems.suggested_fix: None needed for phones. If the owner cares about desktop, the side covers would have to be painted differently during the above-cloud phase, which is outside this lane.

problems.title: T8 left as it was: the cover follows the scene one frame late
problems.where: js/intro.js setSky (called from the intro layer's rAF)
problems.what: This is unchanged and documented. On phones the top 2 px strip changes at the switch frame (744 px) from #0a0c17 (the last band colour) to #090a14, a difference of 1 to 3 per channel. That is invisible, where in the first fix the same strip went navy to black.
problems.evidence: From out/cur.jsonl, chgOut at the switch: 744 px at 360x740 (2976 device px at DPR 2) and 5980 px at 1280x800 (the top 7 px strip). The step at the frame before the switch is 2 to 3 per channel.

per_fix:
Each line: finding -> reproduced before the repair -> gone after -> check that fails when the fix is reverted.

- T1 (near-full-screen navy around 1.0 to 1.3 s)
  - Before: reproduced on the first-fix tree. 360x740 day clear 92.1 % navy at 1.08 s, at or above 90 % for 0.183 s. Whole 1280 window 97.6 %, 0.467 s (out/first.jsonl).
  - After, phones: 360x740 largest one-colour share = the opening frame (73.5 to 78.7 %). Night dark at 1.98 s reaches 78.2 to 78.4 %. Never 90 % at any size or hour.
  - After, 1280 whole window: peak = opening frame (92.1 to 92.6 %; night 94.0 % against base 93.9 %).
  - Guard: the one-colour share must stay within the opening share + 2 %. Mutant k1 (CLOUD.gap = []) fails at 94.1 % / 93.8 %.

- T2 (straight navy/dark line across the wide-screen side covers)
  - Before: reproduced on the first fix. The side and gap columns jump 36 per channel by day and 27 at dusk in one row, and the jump climbs with the bank (out/first.jsonl stepPreMax, pics/r-1280-day-first-vs-now.png).
  - After: largest per-row step 5 to 6 per channel in every look. At the 1280 switch only a 7 px strip changes, #0a0c17 to #090a14 (5980 px). I checked this by eye in pics/r-1280-duskrain-now-1.60.png and -first-1.60.png.
  - Guard: the 1.5 s paint check. Failing mutants: k2 (first-fix cover), k11 (skyCut top = y), k15 (side shadows stay navy down to the panel top), k10 (mix order reversed), k3 (one band, at 1280).
  - Gap: k3b (two bands) passes; see R3.

- T3 (step 0 did not notice the panel hiding the room)
  - Before: reproduced. old-mB (panel at z -1.5 with the first-fix test) exit 0.
  - After: the panel hides 0 px.
  - Guard: the panel-hidden re-render. Mutant k4 (z -1.5) fails: the panel hides 17240 / 21291 px and one colour reaches 96.5 / 97.0 %.

- T4 (the paint check read CSS variables, not pixels)
  - Before: reproduced. old-mC (gradient reverted) and old-mD (box-shadow reverted) both exit 0 with the first-fix test.
  - After: the check reads screenshot columns.
  - Guard: k5 (gradient reverted) fails, 359 / 309 gap rows; k6 (box-shadow reverted) fails, 309 side rows at 1280. k6 passes at 360, which is correct because a phone has no side cover.

- T5 (the paint check depended on wall-clock time)
  - Before: reproduced. old-mW (8 s wait) exit 1, '덮개 @ NaN'.
  - After: an 8 s wait before the scan (k7a) and before the paint read (k7b) both exit 0.
  - Guard: k8 (timer stretch removed plus the 8 s wait) fails with the clear message '하늘 단계가 아님 (title)'.
  - Step 0 on the repaired tree passed 5 times in 5 at load 8 to 10.

- T6 (the owner's 2D 'after' picture showed reverted code)
  - Before: as the first checker reported (sheet time 22:17:28, revert 22:17:40).
  - After: repair-thin/pics/sheet-2d-360x740.png has rows 'before (b287a11)' and 'now'. I looked at it and they match. The 2D code is untouched in the diff. The shared setSky clears its new variables when there is no skyCut (2D has none).
  - Guard: none; this was a picture.

- T7 (nit: rain start and bank bottom not guarded)
  - The bank's bottom edge (dn) is now guarded indirectly. Mutant k9 (dn = 0) fails at 99.7 % dark at 1.80 s.
  - The rain start height is still not measured in pixels. The rainTop code is unchanged.

- T8 (nit: cover one frame late)
  - Left as it was, now harmless; see R5.

The new step 0 is deterministic under load: 5 of 5 passed, and wall-clock waits of 8 s do not change the result.

Steps 1 to 6 of the full intro test: no verdict because of load, and the control died the same way.
Not every hour and weather at every size: I measured 27 of 96 looks (360x740 at all 4 hours with several weathers; 1280 at all 4 hours; 2 to 4 looks for each of the other sizes).
The 2D intro frames myself: I relied on the repair's before/now sheet (it matches) and on the code diff.
